steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add potatoes and cook until tender but still firm, about 45 minutes; drain.
Stir in butter, cheese, garlic, salt, and oregano. Mash with a potato masher or with an electric mixer.

raw_recipe.headline: Garlic Mashed Potatoes Secret Recipe
raw_recipe.description: Red potatoes mashed with butter, Romano cheese, garlic, salt and oregano. A new twist on a familiar favorite!
raw_recipe.name: Garlic Mashed Potatoes Secret Recipe

recipeInstructions.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add potatoes and cook until tender but still firm, about 45 minutes; drain.
Stir in butter, cheese, garlic, salt, and oregano. Mash with a potato masher or with an electric mixer.

review.reviewBody: I'm the author of this recipe, and I just wanted a add a couple of notes. Do NOT use margarine with the recipe, they will come out dry. Make sure you drain the potatoes very well, drop the butter in first, give it a couple of mashes and add the rest of the ingredients. This will help with the consistency. Do NOT overmash or they will get sticky. There should be a few small chunks of potato in the mix when you are done. I know a lot of people do not like raw garlic (I do!), as other reviewers have noted, you may like it better with roasted garlic. Do not add the garlic to the boiling potato water, or you'll end up with almost no garlic flavor at the end. When scaling the recipe, use the "scale recipe" feature on the recipe page to reduce the chance of any math errors. IF you decide to reduce the butter and add milk... the milk MUST be added after you mash in the butter, or the butter will not bind properly with the starch in the potatoes and you'll end up with a weird consistency.

One more review hardly seems worth it - so many have already praised this dish. But I'm adding my 2 cents anyhow: Very good - VERY garlicky. 
I, too, scaled it down for 10 people. Red potatoes boil up very nicely and make it easy to use your blender on them once they're done. I very much liked the strong garlic taste - but a few of my guests did not. However, one did ask for the recipe, and that rarely happens. I did not use quite so much butter as the recipe wanted - I used 2 sticks for the 5 lb of potatoes. After all was said and done, it was more like creamed potatoes than mashed. But I liked it a lot. 
My suggestion on the garlic: next time I make these, I plan on blanching (boiling) the garlic. This, too, will cut down on the rawness of it without killing the flavor. I would suggest putting in the garlic with the boiling potatoes during the last 10 min of boling as this would both flavor the potatoes and tone down the garlic as well.

My daughter made these potatoes to see if they were as good as my garlic mashed potatoes--we both agreed it was a big dud. It would be infinitely better if you put the whole garlic cloves in the water with the potatoes as they cook. This infuses the potatoes with lots of garlic flavor, and the cloves mash right into the potatoes. Also, oregano in mashed potatoes is just not good at all. We didn't even finish the 4 servings it was scaled down to!

Back in the day when allrecipes had a great device to size down the recipe to however many servings you wanted..... Here is for 3lbs of potatoes - 1/2lb butter, 3oz grated cheese, 2T & 2 3/4 t garlic, 1 1/2 t salt, 1 1/2 t dried oregano. Hope this helps someone. Even 3lbs of potatoes is alot. I really really miss that feature where even one serving would be calculated for you. This recipe is fantastic.

Hope this helps since I haven’t seen any real helpful scaled down recipes. The first time I made I didn’t write down the scaled down version since it was easily available via this site. Had I know it was going away I would have written it down. Hope this helps others! Good luck! Scaled Recipe for 10 Servings: • 5 pounds of unpeeled red potatoes • 0.8 pounds (12.8 ounces or about 1¾ cups) of butter • 0.3 pounds (4.8 ounces or about 1⅓ cups grated) of Romano cheese • 0.3 cups (about 5 tablespoons) of chopped garlic • 0.05 cups (about 2.4 teaspoons) of salt • 0.05 cups (about 2.4 teaspoons) of dried oregano
overall it was good. it did make a difference adding the butter in first, mash a bit and then adding the rest. I used yellow potatoes, not red and used my instant pot (8 mins)

Good flavor. Will use a little less cheese next time. Also follow review to not over mix. Would not user a mixer again, just an old fashioned masher. Used proportions from video: 1 1/4 lbs potatoes, 6 tbsp butter, 1/4 c. romano (used 1/4 + 1/8 but will reduce next time), 1 tbsp garlic, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp oregano

First I cut this down to 10 servings which is 5 lbs. I first cut the top off of a large head of garlic, removed papery exterior, placed in tin foil, drizzled with a little oil olive, a pinch of salt, wrapped up tight and cooked in a 375 degree oven for approx. 35 minutes.

I melt butter in small cook pot and put whole peeled cloves in the butter and let simmer gently til cloves are soft. Mash garlic into the butter, and add with grated cheese ( or milk). I find cheese masks the flavour of garlic. And I don’t want that at all!❤️🇨🇦❤️

PROTIP: Use chat gpt to adjust this recipe to however many lbs of potatoes you're using. LOVE this recipe. Here's the adjusted ingredients for 5 lbs if you don't know how to do that: 5 pounds unpeeled red potatoes, quartered 0.8 pounds (about 12.8 ounces or roughly 363 grams) butter, room temperature 0.3 pounds (about 4.8 ounces or roughly 136 grams) Romano cheese, grated 0.3 cups (about 2 tablespoons plus 2 teaspoons) chopped garlic 0.05 cups (about 2.4 teaspoons) salt 0.05 cups (about 2.4 teaspoons) dried oregano

Here is the breakdown from "Recipe Resizer" for 10 servings. 5 lbs unpeeled red potatoes, 12¾ oz butter, 4¾ oz grated Romano cheese, ¼ cup 1 tbsp chopped garlic, 1 tbsp salt, 1 tbsp dried oregano. I used fresh garlic baked (as other users recommended), added Sour Cream (3/4 cup), also used a mixture of my favorite cheeses not just Romano.
Easy to make and tastes great!
The recipe is fine, but the serving size is too much and should be changed to 10 or 20 servings instead of 100.

My potatoes came out a little thick. I feel it may have been missing some heavy cream or milk. I also had trouble bringing down the recipe to 5lb of potatoes. I didn't see a place to do that on this page.
Wow so amazing!!! Used roasted garlic instead of raw. recipe is so yummy! A++++++
I baked the garlic as recommended in a previous suggestion. They were amazing. Everyone in the family loved them, and that itself is miraculous alone. A new family favorite.
I love this recipe, but haven't made it in a while and was dismayed to find I CANNOT adjust it down. Page just doesn't respond. Had to calculate it out myself. Hope it comes out right!
Excellent recipe! I added sour cream & it was so delicious!
